title.rendered: Kindness: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 5

excerpt.rendered: They dragged her into the Temple courts. The Pharisees had caught her in adultery. Jesus knelt down and wrote in the dust. What He did that morning is what the Holy Spirit is producing in you.

content.rendered:
They dragged her into the Temple courts and stood her in the middle of the crowd. The Pharisees had caught her in adultery. The Law was clear. She should be stoned. Jesus knelt down and wrote in the dust. What He did that morning is what the Holy Spirit is producing in you.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, September 28, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 5

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Early one morning in the Temple courts in Jerusalem, a crowd gathered around a rabbi from Nazareth. He was teaching. And into the middle of the teaching, the scribes and Pharisees dragged a woman. She had been caught in the act of adultery. Under the Law of Moses, she should be stoned. They stood her in front of everyone, humiliated, half-dressed, terrified, and put the question to Jesus. “Moses, in the law, commanded us that such should be stoned. But what do You say?” It was a trap. If Jesus said, “Do not stone her,” He was defying the Law of Moses. If He said, “Stone her,” He was contradicting the mercy He had preached for three years. And John tells us Jesus did the most unexpected thing. He knelt down. He wrote in the dust with His finger. And when they kept pressing Him, He stood up and said the sentence that has echoed through two thousand years of Christian preaching. “He who is without sin among you, let him throw a stone at her first.”

One by one, from the oldest to the youngest, the accusers walked away. When Jesus stood up again, only the woman remained. He asked her, “Woman, where are those accusers of yours? Has no one condemned you?” She answered, “No one, Lord.” And Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more.” What Jesus showed the woman in that moment was chrēstotēs. The Greek word for the fifth fruit of the Spirit. Kindness. Not sentimentality. Not weakness. A kindness that refused to condemn what the Law would have condemned, and yet did not indulge what the woman needed to leave behind. Truth and grace, held together in a single word to a single trembling woman. That is the kindness the Holy Spirit is producing in every believer.

The Passion Translation opens up the character of the fruit: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action, a life full of virtue, faith that prevails, gentleness of heart, and strength of spirit” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Kindness in action. Not kindness as a feeling. Not kindness as a nice tone of voice. Kindness that actively steps into a situation and treats the person in it with mercy. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness), peace, patience (an even temper, forbearance), kindness” (Galatians 5:22 AMPC).

The Greek word chrēstotēs is closely related to Christos, the Greek word for Christ. The early Christians noticed the wordplay and made it a testimony. To be Christian was to be Christ-like. And to be Christ-like was to be kind in the specific way Jesus was kind. Not naive. Not soft on sin. But refusing to condemn what grace has released, and refusing to indulge what grace has come to change. That kind of kindness has changed more lives than a thousand well-argued sermons. It is what the woman experienced in the Temple courts that morning. It is what the Holy Spirit produces in the believer who has been rooted in Christ.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the fruit the Spirit is growing in you. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, there is a person in your life who has failed and knows it. Someone who is waiting for the stone. Do not throw it. Do what Jesus did. Speak the kindness of the Kingdom over them. Refuse to condemn what God has come to redeem. Refuse to indulge what God has come to change. Truth and grace, together, in your voice today. That is the kindness the Spirit is producing in you. Walk in it.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that kindness is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Jesus modelled it perfectly in the Temple courts with the woman caught in adultery. Truth and grace, held together in a single kind sentence. Today I ask You to produce that same kindness in me. When someone in my life fails, I refuse to throw the stone. I speak the kindness of the Kingdom over them. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Kindness is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. I refuse to throw the stone. I speak Christ-like kindness over the failing, the struggling, the trembling. Truth and grace, together, in my voice.
